target.title: docs: map the algorithmic closure system
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper has review caching, scheduler policy, repair automation, action receipts, and Gitcrawl integration, but no single numbered system map explaining how those algorithms combine to reduce review and closure latency without weakening apply safety.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the requested #1-6 architecture: semantic identity and Tree-sitter expansion, dependency-graph closure planning, congestion-aware admission, event-sourced actions/reviews/review logs, mutation recovery, and Gitcrawl local/cloud/parity evidence. It also inventories every review, command, dispatch, repair, apply, proof, evidence, and projection action family and states which layer may authorize what.

## User Impact

Maintainers and contributors get one durable design reference for implementing, reviewing, measuring, and rolling back the algorithmic closure stack. This is documentation-only and changes no production behavior.

## Evidence

- exact `origin/main` base `ecc6d03d1ec73267d434cb1905cfc216c78fcd70`
- `git diff --check` passes
- new README and orchestration links resolve to `docs/algorithmic-closure-system.md`
- no changelog change for documentation-only architecture work
- implementation PRs remain separately gated by exact ClawSweeper review and CI; this PR will rebase after that stack lands

target.title: feat(repair): record authoritative dispatch receipts
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/558

## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper dispatch lanes could record incomplete request identities, fail outside GitHub Actions, lose cursor progress after a receipt publication failure, or bypass authoritative receipts in the production dashboard Worker. Workflow publication also used the wrong repository credentials and could suppress unrelated activity forwarding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dispatch receipts now bind every transmitted requeue input and support persistent local producer contexts for the documented comment-webhook and executing self-heal commands. Workflow fixes add the sparse state hydrator, use state-repository credentials, keep activity forwarding independent while surfacing ledger failures, and publish fanout checkpoints even when receipt finalization fails.

Both shared dispatch wrappers now treat successful transport as terminal when accepted-outcome receipt persistence fails: the durability failure is logged, chain state is released, and the original sync or async transport result is returned. Attempt creation remains fail-closed, while rejected and unknown transport outcomes retain their existing strict persistence semantics. Target fanout advances its cursor without replaying an accepted dispatch, and the comment webhook returns its accepted response without triggering redelivery.

The setup-action-ledger composite action now exports a canonical `CLAWSWEEPER_ACTION_LEDGER_ROOT` derived from its workspace-relative `worktree-path`, rejecting missing, absolute, or workspace-escaping roots. Executing self-heal therefore receives a valid durable receipt context in GitHub Actions.

The dashboard Worker routes hosted comment dispatch through the ExactReviewQueue Durable Object and records digest-only SQLite attempt/outcome chains for both comment and item repository dispatches. Dispatch input digests reuse the shared action-ledger credential-field validator after the existing flat and size bounds. Raw payloads, comments, prompts, and credentials are not retained.

The branch remains stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/558 so immutable requeue inputs and dispatch receipts share one recovery contract.

## User Impact

Maintainers get an authoritative audit trail for Actions, documented local repair commands, scheduled fanout, and production webhook dispatches. Ambiguous sends remain visible as unknown, accepted sends are not duplicated after receipt persistence failure, successful fanout selection is not replayed, webhook deliveries are not retried after accepted transport, and executing self-heal has a canonical Actions ledger root.

## Evidence

Final head: `24bf3236b94e18b70f1b02a325357b25bdcb616d`

- deterministic sync and async failure injection proves accepted transport results survive outcome persistence failure and dispatch chain state is released
- deterministic target-fanout regression proves cursor progress advances across two accepted sends instead of replaying the first target
- deterministic comment-webhook regression proves accepted transport returns HTTP 202 with one dispatch and no redelivery/report failure
- attempt-write regressions prove sync and async transport remain fail-closed before dispatch
- Actions-context self-heal regression proves attempt and accepted receipts are emitted with the canonical setup-action-ledger root
- credential alias regressions reject `api_key`, `access_token`, `client_secret`, and `password`
- `node --test test/repair/dispatch-action-receipts.test.ts`: 17 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/repair/target-fanout.test.ts`: 10 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/repair/comment-webhook.test.ts`: 30 passed, 0 failed

- `node --test test/repair/*.test.ts dist/repair/*.test.js`: 801 passed, 0 failed
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.repair.json`: passed

- `oxlint` passed for `src/repair` and `test/repair` with warnings denied
